symptom: `mxcli git doctor` on a fresh clone (or any CI checkout) reports every commit as `[ ] <sha> without a note` and exits 1, while the same report says `[x] origin has refs/notes/mx_metadata`; `--fix` then writes computed notes over commits the remote already annotates, and the `git push origin <branch> refs/notes/mx_metadata` it tells you to run is rejected as non-fast-forward
cause: doctorNotes judged each commit against the LOCAL refs/notes/mx_metadata only, and nothing fetched it: git clone and a plain git fetch never fetch refs/notes/*. The remote check had already run `git ls-remote <remote> refs/notes/mx_metadata` and printed the tip, but that result was not passed on, so an empty local ref read as 'no commit has a note'
file: `cmd/mxcli/gitdoctor.go` (`doctorRun` passes the remote's notes commit to `doctorNotes`; `hasNotesCommit`: the local ref is, or descends from, that commit); test `TestGitDoctor_UnfetchedNotesAreNotMissing` in `cmd/mxcli/gitdoctor_test.go`
insight: **Every existing notes test built its repository with `git init`, never `git clone`**, so the local notes ref was always the only one there was; the defect lives exactly in the gap between a repository that writes notes and one that receives them. A fixture with a bare remote, a pushed note and a fresh clone reproduced it on the first run. **Do not judge, and do not write, against a ref that is behind the remote**: Studio Pro's own fetch force-replaces the local notes ref with the remote's, so the remote's notes are the ones that count; a note written over a remote-annotated commit is either refused on push or thrown away on Studio Pro's next fetch. **Fetch as a fast-forward only** (`git fetch <remote> refs/notes/mx_metadata:refs/notes/mx_metadata`, no `+`): it never discards a note that exists only locally, which a force-fetch would; when the local ref has diverged the fetch is refused and the doctor says so instead of writing. Report mode stays read-only: it names the unfetched ref and the command rather than fetching
